structure: Part 4 read the whole commodities feature folder of the high-risk plants set (src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/commodities/): page.js, fields.js, entry-index.js, evaluation.js, links.js, line-form.js; list/list.controller.js, list/list.njk, list/_cells.njk, list/table-rows.js and their unit tests (list.controller.test.js, table-rows.test.js); details/details.controller.js, details/details.njk and details.controller.test.js; copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and copy/copy.test.js; and fit/list.fit.spec.js (12 tests in two describes) and fit/details.fit.spec.js (18 tests in two describes). For context only it read the set-owned vocabulary service (services/commodities/index.js, claimed by part 3), the commodity obligation section (obligations/sections/commodity.js, claimed by part 12) and src/server/app/shared/kit.js (claimed by part 13), plus the few shared helpers the two pages render through: shared/save-actions.njk, shared/copy.en.js's saveActions block, shared/paths.js's route builders, lib/validate/validators.js's requiredMaxText and requiredIntegerInRange, flow/section-captions/copy/copy.en.js for the caption wording and fit/set-base.js and fit/high-risk-plants-journey.js for the two URL and helper constants its fit specs use. It covers the repeatable commodity collection as a user meets it: the commodities list page (slug 'commodities') with its route, caption, heading, table columns, per-row Change and Remove controls, Add another button, empty state, removal banner, save controls and collection floor; the commodities/details sub-page with its route for adding and for editing, its category question and every per-line field with label, hint, widget, width, cap, condition and error message in English and machine-draft Welsh; every validation rule and redirect on either page; the floor obligation and the absence of a ceiling; the four reshaping modules (entry-index.js, links.js, line-form.js, list/table-rows.js) as mechanism claims; and what each of the 30 fit tests proves. It stops at the commodity-type question itself and at the vocabulary service, which part 3 claims, and at the obligation manifest, which part 12 claims.
